title: The Miñiques volcano complex near Chajnantor
caption: The Miñiques volcano complex near the Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A mountainous landscape stretches away as far as the eye can see, under very clear skies. The mound straight ahead is the Miñiques volcano complex, capped with clouds that seem to point up toward the cosmos. The photograph, credited to P. Horálek, was taken in northern Chile.
This is the view a traveller would have driving north toward San Pedro de Atacama. The camera stood some 50 kilometres away from the Chajnantor plateau, where the ALMA observatory is based.

It may come as a surprise that a European observatory works in the northern Chilean desert. But the vast Atacama gives astronomers exactly what they need, which is dry air and very clear skies. The qualities that make this landscape look so empty are the ones that draw telescopes to it.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera in northern Chile. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: This view is close to what a traveller would see, though a camera exposure may bring out more of the stars than the eye can.

explore: ALMA, the observatory on the nearby Chajnantor plateau, is a large array of antennas that studies the sky at millimetre and submillimetre wavelengths, well beyond the colours our eyes can see.
alt: A mountainous desert landscape under a clear sky, with a volcanic mound topped by clouds straight ahead.
